title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', a continuation of La Longue Marche. He is studying the S3-extended profinite Teichmüller tower in genus 0 with 3 points. Π_{0,3}^~ is an extension of a Galois group by the S3-extended π1 of P^1_Q − {0,1,∞}, and M_{0,3}^~ is the corresponding arithmetic extended fundamental group. Earlier on the same sheet he defined 'Teichmüller homomorphisms' (33)–(36), denoted Θ^F_{B'_2}, Θ^F_G, Θ_ρ, Θ_σ. He now wants to identify them with objects from classical moduli theory.

Step 1. He says Θ^F_{B'_2} in (33) is merely technical, or at least subordinate to Θ^F_G in (34).

Step 2. Θ_ρ (35) and Θ_σ (36) are obtained from Θ_G by composing with two homomorphisms Π_{0,3}^~ → M_{0,3}^~. Morally these are sections ('pointés'). They are attached to the two S3-special rational points of M_{0,3}:
- the point 1/2, in the orbit {−1, 2, 1/2}, with stabilizer of order 2;
- the point −j (a primitive 6th root of unity), in the orbit {−j, −j̄}, with stabilizer of order 3.

Step 3, modern reading. P^1 − {0,1,∞} is the Legendre λ-line Y(2), and its quotient by S3 is the j-line M_{1,1}. The two special points are the elliptic points of the j-line:
- λ = 1/2 gives j = 1728, the curve y^2 = x^3 − x with CM by Z[i];
- λ = −ω gives j = 0, the curve y^2 = x^3 − 1 with CM by Z[ω].
ρ and σ are the elliptic elements of order 4 and 6 in SL2(Z), i.e. order 2 and 3 in PSL2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3. T_ρ and T_σ are their centralizers in GL2, namely the CM tori R_{Q(i)/Q}G_m and R_{Q(√−3)/Q}G_m.

Step 4. At the level of group schemes, the two pointings correspond to two splittings of a group M_{ρ,σ} (introduced in his eq. (3)) over T_{ρ,σ} (his eq. (31)), given in (48):
- ψ_ρ(a,b) = (a,b,a);
- ψ_σ(a,b) = (a,b,b).
He warns that ψ_ρ is only defined on the subgroup T'_{ρ,σ} = {(a,b) : det a = det b} (49). This is the fibre product T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ, which he rewrites as T_ρ × N'_σ, with N'_σ presumably the norm-one part of T_σ.

Step 5, next page. He gets Θ_ρ: Π'^~ → T_ρ(Ẑ)/±1. The sign ambiguities of Θ_ρ and Θ_σ match those of Θ_G ('tout se tient'), which forces replacing M_{0,3}^~ by a ±1-extension τ_{1,1}^~ mapping to GL(2,Ẑ). That map should be the fundamental modular representation of the elliptic moduli stack M_{1,1}.

Upshot: the special-point Teichmüller maps should be the Galois characters of the CM elliptic curves with j = 1728 and j = 0, obtained by restricting the modular GL2(Ẑ) representation to the decomposition data at the elliptic points.
errors: The isomorphism T'_{ρ,σ} = T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ ≅ T_ρ × N'_σ is not canonical as written. It needs a choice of splitting of det on T_σ. det: T_σ → G_m is surjective, but the fibre product is a priori only an extension of T_ρ by N'_σ, so the '=' should be read with care.

Because M_{ρ,σ}^{(3)} is defined off-page, the asymmetry is not checkable from this page alone. ψ_ρ requires det a = det b while ψ_σ apparently does not, presumably because the third coordinate is constrained by det c = det b.

ideas.what: Identify the Galois action on the S3-extended π1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} with the modular action of π1(M_{1,1}), via λ-line = Y(2) and S3-quotient = j-line, after a ±1 extension.
ideas.modern_name: Profinite modular/Teichmüller group of M_{1,1} and its outer Galois representation; GL2(Ẑ)-valued fundamental representation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche discuss the Teichmüller tower and M_{1,1} in spirit; this exact formulation is not known to me in print

ideas.what: Homomorphisms ('pointings') from the arithmetic extended group into M_{0,3}^~ attached to the S3-special rational points 1/2 and −j, i.e. the points with nontrivial automorphism groups.
ideas.modern_name: Sections of the fundamental exact sequence at special rational points / elliptic points with automorphisms; Galois action at special points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Nakamura (Galois representations at special points); Lochak–Schneps (order-2 and order-3 relations of GT)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions points with automorphisms in the Teichmüller tower in general terms

ideas.what: Group-scheme splittings ψ_ρ, ψ_σ over the product of CM tori T_ρ × T_σ, with the det-equalizer subgroup T'_{ρ,σ} as the domain of one of them.
ideas.modern_name: Cartan (CM) tori in GL2 centralizing the elliptic elements of order 4 and 6; fibre product over the determinant

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a precise mechanism: the 'Teichmüller homomorphisms' at the two special points are obtained from the global Θ_G by composing with the pointings at 1/2 and −j. These are then expected to factor through the CM tori T_ρ(Ẑ) and T_σ(Ẑ), modulo matching sign ambiguities. This amounts to recovering the CM Galois characters of y^2=x^3−x and y^2=x^3−1 from the Galois action on π1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} via the S3-symmetry. Ihara, Nakamura and others studied Galois actions at special points, so the spirit is known. The specific bookkeeping (splittings ψ_ρ, ψ_σ, the det-equalizer subgroup, the ±1 coherence 'tout se tient') does not seem to be written down in this form.
missed.quote: (35) et (36) s'en déduisent, en les composant avec les deux homomorphismes Π_{0,3}^~ → M_{0,3}^~ ... associés aux points 1/2 et −j
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean structural statement linking GT-type special-point relations (order 2 and 3) to CM Hecke characters through one GL2(Ẑ) representation. It may be of minor interest to people working on GT and on the arithmetic of M_{1,1}.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page reorganizing previously defined homomorphisms. The underlying link between the special points 1/2 and −ω, CM elliptic curves, and the modular representation of M_{1,1} is natural and known in spirit (Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps). Only the specific splitting bookkeeping is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: 'M^{(3)}_{ρ,σ} sur T^{(31)}_{ρ,σ}': the superscripts (3) and (31) are equation references written above the symbols, not part of the notation.
'ou des moins comme' should read 'ou du moins comme'.
'en prenant de sel que' is likely 'en prenant garde que' or similar ('taking care that').
The interlinear '{+quotients+}' above 'Teichmüller' is uncertain; it may be an insertion like 'quotients' or 'qu'ils' qualifying the Teichmüller homomorphisms.
The '548' at the top is Grothendieck's own page numbering; the '490' at the bottom-left is the archive page number.
In (49) the arrow under (a,b) points to 'T_ρ N'_σ', indicating the identification T'_{ρ,σ} ≅ T_ρ × N'_σ.
The final word may not be 'Fin'; it is unclear in the image.
